sec1.titulo: What an update on a number tells the listener
abertura: Someone in the US asks you for an update on how three HR numbers have changed.
Mark the **three** things a good update about a number usually tells the listener.

itens.t: Every figure since the company started
itens.porque: A listener on a call can hold two or three figures. The rest can go in a report.

itens.t: What the number is now
itens.porque: It is the first thing the listener needs to place everything else.

itens.t: When the number changed
itens.porque: Without the period, the listener cannot tell an old problem from a new one.

itens.t: The name of the system the number came from
itens.porque: Useful for a written report. On a call it rarely changes what the listener does.

itens.t: What the number was before
itens.porque: A number on its own says nothing about direction. The starting point shows the change.

itens.t: How you feel about the number, before the figures
itens.porque: Your reading is useful after the figures, marked as yours.

sec1.rationale: Where it started, where it is, and when it changed. The period is the part people most often leave out.

abertura: Choose the better meaning for each expression.

itens.t: to level off
alts: to stop rising or falling and stay about the same
itens.ok: to stop rising or falling and stay about the same

itens.t: the highest figure in two years
alts: the biggest number anyone has recorded in the last two years
the average of the last two years
itens.ok: the biggest number anyone has recorded in the last two years

itens.t: a hybrid schedule
alts: a timetable with some days at home and some at the office
itens.ok: a timetable with some days at home and some at the office

itens.t: so far
to join a team
alts: to become a member of it
to lead it for a short time
itens.ok: to become a member of it

itens.t: fewer

sec3.titulo: A monthly note, for the story
abertura: A monthly note from a customer service team. Read it once, for the story.

doc.titulo: Monthly note -- customer service team, Recife
doc.texto:
Absenteeism in the team reached 6.1% in March, the highest figure in two years. In April the team started a hybrid schedule, and by the end of June the rate was 4.2%. Since July it has leveled off at around 4%.

Overtime is lower too. The team has worked about 20% fewer overtime hours this year than in the same months last year.

Four people have joined the team since June, and none of them has left so far. Two more people start in October.

abertura: Mark the **two** sentences that sum up the note.

itens.t: The team has lost most of its new people.
itens.porque: The opposite: four people have joined since June, and none of them has left.

itens.t: Absenteeism went down after a change in the schedule, and it has stayed lower.
itens.porque: From 6.1% in March to 4.2% by the end of June, after the hybrid schedule started in April, and around 4% since July.

itens.t: Absenteeism has gone up every month this year.
itens.porque: It reached its highest figure in March and then fell.

itens.t: The team will stop the hybrid schedule in October.
itens.porque: October is when two new people start. Nothing is said about stopping the schedule.

itens.t: Overtime is lower this year than last year.
itens.porque: About 20% fewer overtime hours than in the same months last year.

sec3.rationale: The story is a peak, a change, and a number that has stayed lower since.

sec4.titulo: The time words in the note
abertura: Six time words from the note. Does each one name a period that has ended, or a period that continues until today?
opcoes: a period that continues until today

itens.t: since July
itens.ok: a period that continues until today
itens.porque: From July until the day the note was written.

itens.t: in March
itens.porque: March is over. The note says what the rate was then.

itens.t: by the end of June
itens.porque: The end of June is a point in the past.

itens.t: this year
itens.ok: a period that continues until today
itens.porque: The year is not over when the note is written.

itens.t: since June
itens.ok: a period that continues until today
itens.porque: From June until now, and the note adds so far.

itens.t: in the same months last year
itens.porque: Last year is over.

sec4.rationale: Three of each. Look back at the verb next to each time word in the note.

abertura: Look at the note and at the time words again. Mark the **two** sentences that describe what you can see in the note.

itens.t: Next to “in March”, the verb is *reached*, and next to “since July”, it is *has leveled off*.
itens.porque: Both are in the first paragraph: “reached 6.1% in March” and “Since July it has leveled off”.

itens.t: Every sentence in the note uses the same verb form.
itens.porque: The note has at least two forms: reached, started, was, and has leveled off, has worked, have joined.

itens.t: The verb next to “this year” and “since June” has *has* or *have* in it.
itens.porque: “has worked … this year” and “have joined the team since June”.

itens.t: The note never gives a number from the past.
itens.porque: It gives several: 6.1% in March, 4.2% by the end of June.

sec5.rationale: In this note, the time word and the verb form seem to go together.

abertura: Complete each sentence about the note. You can use these words whenever you describe how a number changed.
itens: "By the end of June it was down {to|90px} 4.2%."

opcoes: a period that is still open

itens.t: "It has gone up again since July."
itens.ok: a period that is still open
itens.porque: From July until today. The rise is still part of the present picture.

itens.t: "Turnover rose from 9.2% to 14.6% in the second quarter."
itens.porque: The second quarter has ended. The sentence reports what happened inside it.

itens.t: "We hired 40 people in May."
itens.porque: May is finished. The hiring happened then.

itens.t: "So far, 22 of them have stayed."
itens.ok: a period that is still open
itens.porque: So far means until now, and the number can still change tomorrow.

itens.t: "Absenteeism has not moved much this year."
itens.ok: a period that is still open
itens.porque: The year is not over, so the sentence covers January until today.

itens.t: "Overtime went from 13 to 30 hours a week between January and June."
itens.porque: January to June is a closed stretch of time. What happened after June is a different sentence.

pd6.rationale: Three of each. The time words in each sentence already say whether the period is over.

itens: "Since July, it {has gone up|150px} (go up) again."
"Overtime {went|100px} (go) from 13 to 30 hours a week between January and June."

callout.texto: Before you choose the verb, ask: is the period I am talking about over? If it is, the past simple usually fits. If it runs until today, the present perfect usually fits.
